name: Filesystem
description: Read, write, search, and manage files and directories on your Mac
setupInstructions: Requires Node.js 18+. Install from https://nodejs.org or run: brew install node. The ~ argument grants access to your home folder — change it to a specific path to restrict access (e.g. ~/Documents).

name: Memory
description: Persistent knowledge graph that remembers facts, preferences, and context across conversations
setupInstructions: Requires Node.js 18+. No additional setup needed. Memory is stored locally in a JSON file in your home directory. The agent can create entities, add observations, and build relationships between concepts.

name: Brave Search
description: Search the web using Brave Search — get current information, news, and answers
setupInstructions: 1. Go to https://brave.com/search/api/ and sign up for a free API key (2,000 queries/month free). 2. Copy your API key. 3. Paste it into the BRAVE_API_KEY field when adding this server.

name: Tavily Search
description: AI-optimized web search — returns clean, structured answers instead of raw links
setupInstructions: 1. Go to https://tavily.com and sign up for a free account (1,000 searches/month free). 2. Copy your API key from the dashboard. 3. Paste it into the TAVILY_API_KEY field. Tavily is built specifically for AI agents — it returns clean, summarized content rather than raw HTML, making it ideal for research tasks.

name: Fetch
description: Fetch and read web pages, articles, and API responses from any URL
setupInstructions: This is a Python server. Requires Python 3.10+ and uvx. Install uvx: brew install uv (or pip install uv). The server fetches web pages and converts them to readable text for the agent.

name: Sequential Thinking
description: Helps the agent think through complex problems step by step with structured reasoning
setupInstructions: Requires Node.js 18+. No additional setup needed. This server provides a structured thinking tool that helps agents break down complex problems, revise their reasoning, and reach better conclusions.

name: Browser Automation
description: Control a web browser — navigate pages, fill forms, click buttons, take screenshots
setupInstructions: Requires Node.js 18+. On first run, Playwright will download a Chromium browser (~150MB). Remove --headless from arguments to see the browser window during automation. Use this for web scraping, form filling, and testing.

name: GitHub
description: Browse repos, create issues, review pull requests, and manage GitHub projects
setupInstructions: 1. Go to https://github.com/settings/tokens and create a Personal Access Token (classic). 2. Select scopes: repo, read:org, read:user. 3. Copy the token and paste it into the GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN field.

name: Slack
description: Read and send Slack messages, search conversations, and manage channels
setupInstructions: 1. Go to https://api.slack.com/apps and click 'Create New App' > 'From scratch'. 2. Under OAuth & Permissions, add Bot Token Scopes: channels:history, channels:read, chat:write, users:read. 3. Install to your workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token (starts with xoxb-). 4. Find your Team ID: open Slack in a browser, it's the T-prefixed code in the URL (e.g. T01234ABCD). 5. Paste both values when adding this server.

name: Notion
description: Search, read, and create pages in your Notion workspace — notes, databases, and wikis
setupInstructions: 1. Go to https://www.notion.so/my-integrations and create a new integration. 2. Copy the Internal Integration Secret (starts with ntn_). 3. In Notion, share the pages/databases you want accessible with your integration (click Share > Invite > select your integration). 4. Set OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS to: {"Authorization": "Bearer ntn_YOUR_SECRET", "Notion-Version": "2022-06-28"}

name: Obsidian
description: Read, search, and edit notes in your Obsidian vault — your personal knowledge base
setupInstructions: 1. Set OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH to the full path of your Obsidian vault (e.g. /Users/you/Documents/MyVault). 2. No Obsidian plugins needed — this reads the vault files directly. 3. The agent can search notes, read content, create new notes, and edit existing ones.

name: Todoist
description: Manage your Todoist tasks — create, complete, organize, and search across projects
setupInstructions: 1. Open Todoist Settings > Integrations > Developer. 2. Copy your API token. 3. Paste it into the TODOIST_API_TOKEN field. The agent can create tasks, mark them complete, organize by project, and set due dates.

name: Apple Shortcuts
description: Run any Shortcut on your Mac — automate apps, system actions, and workflows
setupInstructions: Requires macOS. No additional setup needed — the server discovers all Shortcuts installed on your Mac. Create Shortcuts in the Shortcuts app, then the agent can run them by name. Great for automating repetitive tasks across apps.
